statements.text: The Pole Star belongs to the Little Dipper and appears nearly fixed, so it marks North.
The Pole Star is a member of the Big Dipper and slowly circles the sky each night.
The Big Dipper itself always sits due South, so it cannot help locate North.

stem: Rupa wants to find North using familiar star patterns. She knows the Big Dipper, the Little Dipper, and the Pole Star.

teacher.key_rationale: The Pole Star is in the Little Dipper and stays nearly fixed, marking North. It is not in the Big Dipper. The Big Dipper helps point toward the Pole Star; it does not sit fixed due South.
